questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The invention of the first steam engine by Thomas Newcomen
How Joseph Black discovered latent heat
The life of James Watt and how he improved the steam engine
The history of the Industrial Revolution in Scotland
questions.explain: The passage covers Watt's early life, career and his improvement of the Newcomen steam engine.

questions.q: What did the arrival of Alexander MacFarlane's instruments allow Watt to do?
options: Train for a full apprenticeship under a London instrument maker
Join the Incorporation of Hammermen and open his own shop
Partner with Matthew Boulton to build the first steam engine
Restore them, get paid, then open a workshop at the university
questions.explain: Watt restored the instruments and was paid, and professors then offered him a small workshop in the university.

Ann MacGregor, a dye-maker's daughter
Agnes Muirhead, daughter of a shipwright
Peggy Craig, the daughter of John Craig
questions.explain: In 1764 Watt married his cousin Margaret (Peggy) Miller.

questions.q: About how much of the steam's thermal energy did Watt find was used heating the cylinder each cycle?
options: One-quarter
Half
Nine-tenths
Three-quarters
questions.explain: Watt showed about three-quarters of the steam's thermal energy was consumed heating the cylinder each cycle.

questions.q: What does the passage suggest about the story of Watt and the kettle?
options: Watt invented the steam engine after watching a kettle as a boy
Probably a myth, though he did use a kettle in experiments
It was first told by Watt himself in his surviving diaries
It proves Watt never studied the thermodynamics of steam
questions.explain: The passage calls it apocryphal in its many versions but notes his diaries show he used a kettle as a boiler.
